stem: Having chosen not to rely on any runtime mitigation, a team wants to rigorously correct measurement (readout) error in their SamplerV2 counts — not merely post-select. Which do-it-yourself technique fits the raw per-shot data the Sampler provides?

options.text: Invert an assignment (confusion) matrix measured from calibration circuits (e.g. with M3)
Raise `sampler.options.resilience_level` until the readout error is mitigated away
Apply Zero-Noise Extrapolation to the returned bitstrings, extrapolating each shot to the zero-noise limit
Enable gate twirling, which measures and then inverts the readout confusion matrix for you

explanation.correct: Readout error is a classical relabeling of measured bits, captured by an assignment/confusion matrix that you measure with calibration circuits (prepare each basis state, record what you read back). Inverting — or least-squares inverting — that matrix corrects the counts. The Sampler's raw per-shot data is exactly the input such a method needs, which is why this correction is done by you in post-processing (with your own code or an external package such as mthree/M3), not by a runtime option: the Sampler's own noise-management options are dynamical decoupling and Pauli twirling only.

distractors.B: SamplerV2 has no `resilience_level` — the assignment raises — and a resilience level would not build a readout-calibration matrix in any case.
distractors.C: Zero-Noise Extrapolation mitigates *expectation values* by amplifying gate noise and extrapolating; it is not defined on individual sampled bitstrings.
distractors.D: Twirling randomizes coherent gate/measurement noise into a simpler stochastic form; it neither measures nor inverts the readout confusion matrix.

provenance.notes: s5 adversarial review: high-severity length tell fixed; resilience ruling: distractor B names resilience_level as Estimator-only; added the Sampler noise-management guide as the authoritative citation for the DD/twirling-only option set
